results.title: Conditional Access requires MFA for all users
results.why: Without a tenant-wide MFA policy, one phished password is a full account takeover.
results.fix: Create an enabled Conditional Access policy for All users and All cloud apps that requires MFA (or an authentication strength); exclude only break-glass accounts.

results.title: Legacy authentication is blocked
results.why: Legacy protocols (IMAP, POP, SMTP AUTH, older Office clients) cannot do MFA, so they bypass it.
results.fix: Enable a Conditional Access policy for All users with client apps 'Exchange ActiveSync' and 'Other clients' and grant control 'Block'.

findings.detail: A legacy-auth block policy exists but is not enforced: 'CA002 Block legacy authentication' (enabledForReportingButNotEnforced).

results.title: Administrators must use phishing-resistant MFA
results.why: Push and code-based MFA can be relayed by adversary-in-the-middle phishing kits; FIDO2 and Windows Hello cannot.
results.fix: Require the built-in 'Phishing-resistant MFA' authentication strength for privileged directory roles.

results.title: No Conditional Access policies left in report-only or disabled
results.why: Report-only and disabled policies look like protection on a dashboard but enforce nothing.
results.fix: Review sign-in impact in report-only mode, then switch the policy to On, or delete it.

findings.resource: CA004 Require compliant device for Exchange Online

results.title: Between two and four Global Administrators
results.why: Microsoft recommends fewer than five Global Administrators; more widens the blast radius of a compromise, and fewer than two risks lockout.
results.fix: Move day-to-day admins to least-privileged roles and keep two break-glass Global Administrators.

findings.detail: 5 permanent Global Administrators: aisha.khan@contosofield.example, break-glass-01@contosofield.example, maria.lopez@contosofield.example, old.admin@contosofield.example, tom.becker@contosofield.example.

results.title: Privileged roles are PIM-eligible, not permanent
results.why: Standing admin rights are always available to an attacker; just-in-time activation limits the window.
results.fix: Convert permanent privileged assignments to eligible assignments in Privileged Identity Management, keeping only break-glass accounts permanent.

results.title: Every privileged user has MFA registered
results.why: A privileged account with no MFA method can be registered by whoever signs in first, including an attacker.
results.fix: Require MFA registration for the account now, and block sign-in until it is done.

results.title: No enabled accounts inactive for 90 days
results.why: Unused accounts are rarely monitored, so they are a common foothold.
results.fix: Disable accounts with no sign-in for 90 days after confirming with the owner; review service accounts separately.

findings.detail: enabled and has never signed in

results.title: No guest accounts hold privileged roles
results.why: Guests are governed by another organization's identity controls and offboarding.
results.fix: Remove the role, or give the person a member account governed by your own policies.

results.title: Users cannot consent to applications on their own
results.why: Illicit consent grants give an attacker's app persistent mailbox or file access that survives a password reset.
results.fix: Set user consent to 'Do not allow' (or verified publishers with low-risk permissions only) and turn on the admin consent workflow.

results.title: No app secrets expired or expiring within 30 days
results.why: Expired secrets break integrations; expiring ones get rotated in a hurry.
results.fix: Rotate the secret, or better, move the app to a certificate or managed identity.

results.title: App secrets are valid for no more than 365 days
results.why: Long-lived secrets are the ones that end up in scripts and repositories.
results.fix: Issue secrets for 12 months or less, or replace them with certificates or managed identities.

results.title: No apps hold high-risk Microsoft Graph application permissions
results.why: Application permissions act without a signed-in user; Directory.ReadWrite.All or Mail.ReadWrite on a compromised app is tenant-wide.
results.fix: Replace with least-privilege or resource-scoped permissions (for mail, an Exchange application access policy or RBAC for Applications), and review owners and credentials of apps that keep them.

results.title: No SSH or RDP open to the internet
results.why: Internet-exposed management ports are brute-forced within minutes of exposure.
results.fix: Remove the rule and use Azure Bastion or just-in-time VM access; if a rule must stay, restrict the source.

results.title: Storage accounts block anonymous blob access
results.why: Anonymous access exposes any container someone later marks public.
results.fix: Set allowBlobPublicAccess to false on the account.

results.title: Storage accounts require TLS 1.2 or later
results.why: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated and have known weaknesses.
results.fix: Set minimumTlsVersion to TLS1_2.

results.title: Storage accounts accept HTTPS only
results.why: Plain HTTP exposes data and shared access signatures in transit.
results.fix: Set supportsHttpsTrafficOnly to true.

results.title: Storage accounts disable shared key authorization
results.why: Account keys grant full access and bypass Entra ID, Conditional Access, and per-user audit.
results.fix: Move clients to Entra ID authorization, then set allowSharedKeyAccess to false.

results.title: Key vaults have purge protection
results.why: Without purge protection, a deleted vault or key can be permanently destroyed during the retention window.
results.fix: Enable purge protection (it cannot be turned off afterwards).

results.title: Key vaults are not reachable from public networks
results.why: Secrets should be reachable only from the networks that use them.
results.fix: Disable public network access and use a private endpoint, or restrict the firewall to known networks.

results.title: SQL servers are not reachable from public networks
results.why: Public endpoints expose the database login surface to the internet.
results.fix: Disable public network access and connect through a private endpoint.

results.title: SQL server auditing is enabled
results.why: Without auditing there is no record of who queried or changed data.
results.fix: Enable server-level auditing to a Log Analytics workspace.

results.title: Subscription activity log is sent to Log Analytics
results.why: The activity log is kept for 90 days and can't be queried with other telemetry unless it is exported.
results.fix: Add a subscription diagnostic setting that sends Administrative, Security and Policy logs to the Sentinel workspace.

results.title: Defender for Cloud plans are on for core workloads
results.why: The free tier gives posture recommendations only; threat detection needs the paid plan per resource type.
results.fix: Enable the Standard tier for VirtualMachines, SqlServers, StorageAccounts, KeyVaults.
